voices.1: en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural (chosen voice), base rate -8%, directed per passage (render_edge.py)

tracks.room: Plaza Castellana · just inside the gate
tracks.title: Welcome to the Poble Espanyol
tracks.where: In Plaza Castellana, the square just inside the Ávila gate, a few steps in and out of the flow of people coming through.
tracks.what: The Poble Espanyol de Montjuïc ("Spanish Village"), built for the 1929 Barcelona International Exhibition; 117 full-size buildings modelled on originals all over Spain (OFF-op); construction from January 1928, opened 20 May 1929 (OFF-op); meant to be demolished, kept. Official plan Feb 2026: houses numbered 1–116, four region colours, a marked step-free route.
tracks.listen: What this village is, why it is an interpretation and not a set of copies, the loop we walk, the three lengths, and how the guide points you to houses.

tracks.room: Plaza Castellana · facing the gate's two towers
tracks.title: Plaza Castellana — The towers of Ávila
tracks.where: In Plaza Castellana, facing the inner side of the Ávila gate: two round towers with battlements, joined by a walkway; stand back far enough to see both towers and the walkway, clear of people coming in.
tracks.what: The gate, modelled on the Puerta de San Vicente in the medieval walls of Ávila (DOC, PLAN drawing); 1928 archive caption; the 1929 opening by Alfonso XIII and Victoria Eugenia. Around the square, by the Poble's own list: Casa del Sol, Cáceres = house 3 (DOC, EST); Golfines de Abajo, Carvajal, Mayoralgo, Hernando de Ovando (Cáceres), Almaraz (Plasencia), Palacio del Obispo (Miajadas) (PIN+COL, numbers not spoken).
tracks.listen: Who posed in front of these towers in 1929, which gate in Ávila they represent, why you have to come in through them, and the Extremadura palaces round the square.

tracks.room: Plaza Castellana · facing the gate (Extra)
tracks.title: Plaza Castellana · Extra · Sun and Moon
tracks.where: In Plaza Castellana, anywhere with the gate's two towers in view; position-free.
tracks.what: The Torres de Ávila night venue inside the gate's towers, designed by Alfredo Arribas and Javier Mariscal, as reported by El Temps, 30 Jul 1990 (the Sun and the Moon; the fibre-optic wall; the terrace); Mariscal's Cobi, the Barcelona 1992 mascot (no creation year spoken: unverified, AUDIT_V5_FACTS S9). The venue's present status is NOT stated.
tracks.listen: How the village tried to learn to live at night in 1990, and the one real thread between this gate and the 1992 Olympics.

tracks.room: Calle Caballeros · at its start, by Plaza Castellana
tracks.title: Calle Caballeros — Four men and a Hispano-Suiza
tracks.where: At the start of Calle Caballeros, where it leaves Plaza Castellana between houses 115 and 2, on the step-free route; stand to one side so the street stays clear.
tracks.what: The research trips of 1927–28: Miquel Utrillo, Xavier Nogués, Francesc Folguera and Ramon Reventós; first trip 2 Sep – 2 Oct 1927 in a Hispano-Suiza (almost 700 towns passed, 137 studied); trips 2 and 3 (Nov 1927, May 1928); the method; the burnt clutch; only 9 preliminary models kept; the five travel notebooks, hidden in a desk drawer in the office of J. M. Reventós (ACE19 p. 239 n. 11; "Private archive of the Reventós family", EGA24), no duration sourced; about a thousand 1927 negatives in the Arxiu Fotogràfic.
tracks.listen: How four men in one car rewrote the village after one month on the road, and how their notebooks stayed hidden in a drawer until researchers found them.

tracks.room: Calle Caballeros · walking up, houses 113 to 103 (heard walking)
tracks.title: Calle Caballeros — Coats of arms
tracks.where: Heard while walking slowly up Calle Caballeros from Plaza Castellana toward the junction with Calle Príncipe de Viana at houses 102/103, on the step-free route; the first part needs no view.
tracks.what: Calle Caballeros, by the Poble's own building list (BDB, all PIN+COL, numbers not spoken): Casa del Doncel (Sigüenza, Guadalajara); Casa de la Torre and Palacio de los Contreras (Ayllón, Segovia); Palacio Episcopal (El Burgo de Osma, Soria); Casa del Segle XV (Segovia); Casa de los Benavides and Casa D. Ramón de la Fuente (Toro, Zamora); Casa del Francés (Molinos de Duero, Soria); Casa Ramos (Vinuesa, Soria); the purple Jérica (Castellón) and Casa Desclergue (Montblanc, Tarragona), pins on 23/24, which sit one row back from the street frontage on the plan; the green Casa del Marqués de Santillana (Santillana del Mar, Cantabria). The Poble's casts of stones and 800,000 old tiles. DATED: craft workshops on the street.
tracks.listen: Whose houses line this street, what the coats of arms were for, and two ways to catch the builders' craft.

tracks.room: Junction of Calle Caballeros and Calle Príncipe de Viana · houses 102/103
tracks.title: Calle Príncipe de Viana — The men who made it
tracks.where: Where Calle Caballeros becomes Calle Príncipe de Viana, by houses 102 and 103, with the Travesía del Maestrazgo going off beside house 41 (an accessible-route marker on the plan); stand to one side for a few minutes. Position-free.
tracks.what: The four makers: Miquel Utrillo (1862–1934), Xavier Nogués (1873–1941), Francesc Folguera (1891–1960), Ramon Reventós (1892–1976); Iberiona (early 1920s), halted by Primo de Rivera's coup of 1923, re-presented in 1926; Maricel (Sitges); Maurice Utrillo's surname; the Teatre Grec; the leftover plot; Mirador, 5 Dec 1929; Arquitectura, 1961. Puig i Cadafalch drew the Exhibition's general plan, not the village.
tracks.listen: Who really made the Poble Espanyol, why even their contemporaries argued about it, and what each of the four brought.

tracks.room: Calle Príncipe de Viana · walking up to Plaza Aragonesa (heard walking)
tracks.title: Calle Príncipe de Viana — Navarre and the Basque hills
tracks.where: Heard while walking up the curving Calle Príncipe de Viana from the junction at 102/103 toward Plaza Aragonesa and the brick tower, on the step-free route; the first part needs no view. The Bajada de Cervantes, a side street of steps, is mentioned but not on the route.
tracks.what: Calle Príncipe de Viana, by the Poble's own building list (BDB, all PIN+COL, numbers not spoken; green on the plan): Palacio de San Cristóbal (Estella), Casa de las Cadenas (Corella), pre-Romanesque reliefs (Villatuerta), the López de Goicoechea coat of arms (Olazagutía), Valle del Roncal (Navarre); Caserío Casa Arteche (Erandio, Bizkaia), Vergara (Gipuzkoa); Palacio de los Álava-Esquivel. The Arco de Maia from Amaiur (Baztán, Navarre), recorded on this street by RAH11/RAH-E, exact place. The eleven small sculptures on the Bajada de Cervantes (school guide, May 2026).
tracks.listen: How the village turns from Castile to Navarre and the Basque Country, with a callback to the burnt clutch, and an arch that belongs to Navarre.

tracks.room: Plaza Aragonesa · the whole tower in view
tracks.title: Plaza Aragonesa — The tower they liked better
tracks.where: In Plaza Aragonesa, at the top of Calle Príncipe de Viana, standing where the whole brick tower is in view; it rises between Plaza Aragonesa and Plaza del Carmen, at the end of the church (57–59 on the plan). The Plaza de la Iglesia is reached along the church front; the Fran Daurel Museum is the grey block on the plan behind the church.
tracks.what: The Poble's tower (DOC, PLAN drawing), modelled on the Mudéjar bell tower of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Utebo (Zaragoza), completed 1544 by Alonso de Leznes; the Poble's version slightly reduced, cast in whole plaster moulds; the church: Carmelite church of Alcañiz façade + Utebo tower + Torralba de Ribota façade (preliminary design Baroque: Amorebieta + Caldes de Montbui). DATED: FIESTA, 10 min, "inside the iconic Utebo Tower" (page mod. 3 Mar 2026).
tracks.listen: Why the travellers came to prefer their own tower to the real one, how one trip to Aragon changed the church, and why the tower is a cast.

tracks.room: Plaza de la Iglesia · facing the church front
tracks.title: Plaza de la Iglesia — A church from three towns
tracks.where: In the Plaza de la Iglesia, reached from Plaza Aragonesa along the church front (57–59 on the plan), the small square where the wide steps of the Gradas de Santiago go down; face the church front, with the brick tower at its far end.
tracks.what: The Poble's church, a composite of three Aragonese models: the façade of the Carmelite church of Alcañiz (Teruel; BDB pin by 57/58, PIN+COL, number not spoken), the Mudéjar bell tower of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción at Utebo (Zaragoza; DOC, plan drawing) and a façade from Torralba de Ribota (near Calatayud, Zaragoza; position not known,). The preliminary design was a Baroque church fusing Amorebieta and Caldes de Montbui. Built 1928–29.
tracks.listen: How one trip to Aragon turned a planned Baroque church into a "symbiosis" of three Aragonese buildings, and the three small squares round it.

tracks.room: The FIESTA door, by the tower (play before going in)
tracks.title: Utebo tower · Extra · FIESTA
tracks.where: At the door of FIESTA by the brick tower, before you go in; play it outside, as there is nothing to hear during the show.
tracks.what: FIESTA, a ten-minute show of light and sound on Spain's festivals (the Castellers, La Patum, the Sanfermines, Andalusian Holy Week), "inside the iconic Utebo Tower" (operator), in a room of about 150 m² and 7 m high; made in 2018 by Mediapro Exhibitions. DATED (FIESTA page mod. 3 Mar 2026).
tracks.listen: The 1929 village as a permanent fiesta, and the ten-minute show that carries that idea today.

tracks.room: Plaza de la Iglesia · by the Fran Daurel Museum door
tracks.title: Plaza de la Iglesia — A bottler's art collection
tracks.where: By the door of the Fran Daurel Museum on the Plaza de la Iglesia; on the plan the museum is the grey block behind the church, between the brick tower and the Guinovart Space (56). Stand to one side of the door.
tracks.what: The Fran Daurel Museum (Fundació Fran Daurel), founded by Francesc Daurella i Franco (born Barcelona 1927; no tense claim), in the Poble since December 2001: more than 300 works by more than 80 artists (Picasso, Miró, Dalí, Tàpies, Barceló, Chillida); twenty Picasso ceramics, two etchings and an engraving from the 1960s; Dalí's bronze "Alice au pays des merveilles" (1970s) and ink drawing "Cavalier avec son aurige"; late Miró lithographs and engravings. Grey on the official plan, outside the four region colours (82 and 89 are grey too; the plan has no grey legend). Works on show:. DATED (DAUREL mod. 25 Sep 2025).
tracks.listen: How a Coca-Cola bottler's collection of Picasso, Miró and Dalí came to sit in a 1929 village, and why it isn't as out of place as it looks.

tracks.room: Carrer de la Davallada · house 83, facing the outside stair
tracks.title: Carrer de la Davallada — Seven steps, not fourteen
tracks.where: On Carrer de la Davallada, the street that climbs from Plaza Aragonesa into the Catalan quarter, in front of house 83, just below where Carrer Mercaders comes in; the house has an outside stair up its front.
tracks.what: House 83, Can Banús, modelled on a house in Rupit (province of Barcelona; DOC: Banús, "el 83 amb el de carrer de la Davallada"). Banús counts eight Rupit houses on five fronts (83 here; 79–82 on Carrer Mercaders, with Can Serra above Can Vázquez at 80 and 81 combining Can Rovira, Can Sallent and Ca l'Estragués) (DOC). The stair: seven steps here, fourteen in Rupit (Banús). Built 1928–29.
tracks.listen: A writer for Rupit's local journal counts the steps of a house from Rupit, and shows the Poble is a version, not a copy.

tracks.room: Carrer Mercaders · house 81
tracks.title: Carrer Mercaders — The glassblower's house
tracks.where: On Carrer Mercaders, the street of Rupit house fronts that leads up from house 83 toward Plaça de la Font, outside house 81, where a glass furnace may be at work; stand clear of the door.
tracks.what: House 81, the composite Rupit house (Banús: elements of several Rupit houses, among them Can Rovira and Can Sallent, and the doorway of Ca l'Estragués; DOC); the glassblower, "House 81" (operator; DATED, mod. 18 Mar 2026; no brand). The crafts (CRAFTS mod. 4 Sep 2026; DATED). Built 1928–29.
tracks.listen: A glass furnace inside a house blended from several in Rupit, and why living crafts were part of the village's idea.

tracks.room: Plaça de la Font · by the fountain
tracks.title: Plaça de la Font — The Mediterranean
tracks.where: In Plaça de la Font, the square at the top of Carrer Mercaders, by its fountain; the Baluard opens off the square.
tracks.what: The Mediterranean zone (purple on the plan): the fountain modelled on one at Prades (Baix Camp) (ENC; position); round the square, by the Poble's list, Cornudella, a house from La Garriga, the Casa dels Balbs, the house of the Marquès de la Floresta (Tàrrega) and La Jana (Castellón) (BDB, PIN+COL, numbers not spoken); house 69 described by the operator as a "Balearic Island-style stately home" (EST); its identification as Casa Son Berga, Palma de Mallorca, is a pin inference (ROUTE §3.4 INF), not spoken as certain; the Prades fountain's position is not sourced. Built 1928–29.
tracks.listen: Why the four Catalans did Catalonia last, what this square brings together, and the Balearic house that came in after all.

tracks.room: Barcelona Panorama · by the Baluard, the city in view
tracks.title: Barcelona Panorama — Born under a dictatorship
tracks.where: At the viewpoint the plan calls Barcelona Panorama, beside the Baluard off Plaça de la Font, with the city spread below you; stand back from the edge. Speak only the landmarks ticked on site. The cue offers the Sculpture Garden Extra to Essential and Full only, and names the step-free path round the houses at the top of Plaça de la Font (ALT-S route).
tracks.what: The view (operator: the Sagrada Família, the Mapfre towers, Tibidabo; each subject to O9). The 1929 International Exhibition on Montjuïc (BIE: "Industry, Art and Sport", over 100 ha, 29 nations, almost 5.8 million visitors, opened 19 May 1929; the village 20 May). The two readings of the village's politics: national unity under Primo de Rivera (Mendelson; Sirés 2010) and the Catalanist makers and earlier idea (Sirés 2010). Version-neutral Franco sentence.
tracks.listen: The 1929 Exhibition that filled this hill, and two honest readings of a village born under a dictatorship.

tracks.room: Sculpture Garden · just inside
tracks.title: Sculpture Garden · Extra · Thirty-six sculptures and two slides
tracks.where: Just inside the Sculpture Garden, below the viewpoint, where the giant slides are; the garden is a dead end, so you come back the same way. The way in is unconfirmed: from the viewpoint and the Baluard, or by the steps beside house 89 at the foot of Carrer Mercaders, where the plan draws the garden path (if so, ALT-G2 in AUDIT_FIXES).
tracks.what: The Sculpture Garden: 36 sculptures by 27 contemporary artists, opened 2004 (operator); listed with the Fundació Fran Daurel (ENC); gentle slopes; two giant slides; a vantage point at the end. No size (sources conflict). Artists named only from labels photographed at O10.
tracks.listen: A garden of twentieth-century sculpture beside a Romanesque monastery, and one label to read for yourself.

tracks.room: Monastery of Sant Miquel · in front of the portal
tracks.title: Monastery of Sant Miquel — A monastery in pieces
tracks.where: At the top of the hill, in front of the arched portal of the Monastery of Sant Miquel, house 116, the Romanesque church with the square bell tower; not step-free.
tracks.what: The Monastery of Sant Miquel (116, DOC), a composite of Catalan Romanesque models (city 2013): portal from Santa Maria de Porqueres (Pla de l'Estany); floor inspired by Sant Sebastià de Montmajor (Caldes de Montbui); cloister modelled on the Benedictine monastery of Sant Benet de Bages (no date for the cloister); bell tower after Sant Genís de Taradell; wall paintings by Rafael Padilla (Málaga, 1878–1961). Built 1928–29 by the Poble's team; partly collapsed 1993, re-inaugurated Oct 1997; interior opened to general visitors 11 Jul 2013 (current access).
tracks.listen: The monastery as a collage of Catalan Romanesque churches, the twentieth-century painter behind its "medieval" walls, and the Poble's own slip about who designed it.

tracks.room: Plaza de la Hermandad · white walls round you
tracks.title: Plaza de la Hermandad — Left out, then added for the King
tracks.where: In the small Plaza de la Hermandad at the top of the Andalusian quarter, where the walls turn white, reached by the path from the monastery past house 69; the Vidre art gallery (67/68) stands on the square.
tracks.what: The Andalusian quarter (the plan's yellow South): left out of the first trip because of Seville's 1929 Ibero-American Exhibition, added and moved within the plan after Alfonso XIII asked about it and the third trip (May 1928, 21 days). Houses from the official list (BDB; numbers PIN+COL, not spoken): Casa-Palacio García de Veas (Arcos de la Frontera, Cádiz; VEAS, three balconies, place by O12), Casa de Nínca (Úbeda, Jaén), Iglesia del Santo Ángel and a patio (Córdoba), Palacio del Marqués de Peñaflor (Écija, Sevilla), Posada de las Ánimas (Ronda, Málaga), Casa de los Celdrán (Murcia). Vidre art gallery, 67/68 (DOC), since Feb 2024 (DATED).
tracks.listen: Why the south was left out of the village, how a king's question brought it in, and what to look for: blue pots and three balconies from Arcos de la Frontera.

tracks.room: Calle Arcos · outside the Tablao de Carmen (house 61, C. Arcos 9)
tracks.title: Calle Arcos · Extra · The flamenco house
tracks.where: On Calle Arcos, in the Andalusian quarter, outside the door of the Tablao de Carmen, house 61 on the plan (one of several 61s along the street) and "C/ Arcos, 9" by its address (FILM-T), neither spoken until O13; stand to one side of the door. Calle Arcos has steps.
tracks.what: The Tablao de Carmen, house 61, C/ Arcos 9 (DOC; TABLAO-OP, FILM-T), flamenco shows since 1988, created as a tribute to Carmen Amaya (died 1963). The venue's story that she danced for Alfonso XIII at the 1929 opening (LEGEND, attributed). The street: Calle Arcos, from Arcos de la Frontera, Cádiz (BDB).
tracks.listen: The flamenco house's story of a girl dancing for the King, told as its story, and what is certain about Carmen Amaya.

tracks.room: Plaza del Carmen · at the foot of the tower (play here or crossing to the Plaza de la Iglesia)
tracks.title: Plaza del Carmen — War, prisoners and a folk museum
tracks.where: In the small Plaza del Carmen at the foot of the brick tower, or walking on past the tower and along the church to the Plaza de la Iglesia and the top of the Gradas de Santiago; the track needs no view. Step-free note: the Gradas de Santiago ahead are steps; the step-free way to the Plaza Mayor goes back across Plaza Aragonesa, down Calle Príncipe de Viana to the junction at 102/103 and along Calle Alcalde de Móstoles into the square.
tracks.what: The Poble from the mid-1930s to the 1990s, told without placing anything in a house: the art museum's library (1934; Olot during the war; back in 1939); the Poble's own account of a "prisoner internment camp" in the war (HEDGE: no side, date or number; not mentioned in ARA's count of sixteen Francoist camps in Catalonia, which names 14 municipalities and covers Francoist camps only); "danger of falling into ruin"; the Museu d'Indústries i Arts Populars (1942), ethnological section by Ramon Violant i Simorra; the Poble's own line on "violently anti-Catalanist messages" (attributed); 1957–73 relaunch; the museums until their merger in 1999.
tracks.listen: What became of the fiesta village between the 1930s and the 1990s: a library, the war, and a folk museum, each told in its source's own words.

tracks.room: Gradas de Santiago · at the top
tracks.title: Gradas de Santiago — The North
tracks.where: At the top of the Gradas de Santiago, the wide flight of steps going down from the Plaza de la Iglesia toward the Plaza Mayor; stand to the side, out of the way of people using the steps. Not step-free: the step-free way to the Plaza Mayor goes back across Plaza Aragonesa, down Calle Príncipe de Viana to the junction at 102/103 and along Calle Alcalde de Móstoles into the square.
tracks.what: The Gradas de Santiago (the EN plan's "Santiago Stands"; no documented model) and the green houses round them. Towns from the official list (BDB; numbers PIN+COL, not spoken): Cambados and the Pazo de Fefiñáns (Pontevedra), Betanzos (A Coruña), Villanueva de Lourenzá (Lugo), Cangas de Onís (Asturias), Arcos de la Lonja (Sos del Rey Católico, Zaragoza), Maluenda (Zaragoza); Caldas de Reyes (Pontevedra) on the list but unplaceable (PIN). No Galician model is documented by the historians (F6.51).
tracks.listen: The least documented corner of the village, said plainly: what the steps are called, which northern towns the Poble's list names, and what nobody has yet matched.

tracks.room: Plaza Mayor · on the steps, the whole square in view
tracks.title: Plaza Mayor — A square from Riaza
tracks.where: On the steps across the Plaza Mayor, the big square with the arcaded town hall (house 21) on one side and the bandstand at the opposite corner; sit or stand where the whole square is in view.
tracks.what: The Plaza Mayor: laid out like the square of Riaza (Segovia), with its changes of level (ACE19, ARQ20); fronts from many towns. On the Plaza Castellana side the town halls of Graus, La Fresneda (Teruel), Sangüesa (Navarre) and Sigüenza (ARQ20; BDB 25–28 PIN+COL, not spoken); on the opposite side, seven models including Riaza's La Casona (most likely house 14, PIN+COL, not spoken); Alquézar (Huesca); Santillana del Mar's Casa de Águila and Casa Barreda (BDB, PIN+COL). Town hall, house 21, modelled on Valderrobres (DOC). About 2,000 m²; concert capacity 5,200 (SQUARE); 1968: the village agreed to hold a yearly festival (BANUS).
tracks.listen: Reventós's delighted note on a house in Riaza, what the square really took from Riaza, and the towns whose fronts surround you.

tracks.room: Town hall (21) · under the arcade, by the exhibition door
tracks.title: Town hall — Valderrobres, and a building site
tracks.where: Under the arcade along the front of the town hall, house 21, the big arcaded building on the Plaza Mayor, beside the door of the photographic exhibition.
tracks.what: House 21 (DOC): the town hall, modelled on the Ayuntamiento of Valderrobres / Vall-de-roures (Matarranya, Teruel, Aragon), Mannerist, finished 1599 (date on the coat of arms), by Antonio de Champanyach (LPMB; not spoken). The Poble's version is clearly larger and freestanding, with a staircase from the monastery of Orihuela and a ceiling pattern from the Audiencia of Valencia (ACE19, ARQ20). Inside: "A photographic journey. The construction of Poble Espanyol" (PHOTO; open status O15). Building site: contract to Material y Obras (Jan 1928), about 2.5 million pesetas (not spoken), work from 19 Jan 1928, over 1,000 workers, opened 20 May 1929.
tracks.listen: The last stage of the first trip, how the Poble's town hall differs from Valderrobres, and how the village was built in little more than a year.

tracks.room: Plaza Mayor · sitting on the steps
tracks.title: Plaza Mayor — An irremediably trivial idea
tracks.where: Sitting on the steps of the Plaza Mayor, anywhere quiet with the square in view (under ALT-X, anywhere quiet at the edge of the square).
tracks.what: What critics thought of the Poble, 1929 to 1961, and its later life: the 1929–30 critics in D'Ací i d'Allà (Just Cabot, Domènec Carles, Carles Soldevila); the "merry-go-round" years; the unsigned 1961 article in Arquitectura (COAM), both halves; Bohigas's "psychological habitability" (not named); 1986 municipal plan and private management (Maragall, 30-year concession); the 1990 bar in the gate; losses and the 1996 suspension of payments; the 1996 take-over; 2017 visitors (DATED).
tracks.listen: How the village went from admired to dismissed to studied, in the critics' own words, and how it nearly failed again before it recovered.

tracks.room: Plaza Mayor · by the arcade at 26, the gate beyond
tracks.title: Plaza Mayor — The village that stayed
tracks.where: At the corner of the Plaza Mayor by the arcade at house 26, the passage through to Plaza Castellana, with the Ávila gate just beyond; stand clear of the passage. The way out is the Ávila gate, the way you came in.
tracks.what: Close of the tour. Anton Vidal, the Poble's director general, 2018; built as a temporary set, now a Bé Cultural d'Interès Local; the researchers' view that the trips saved it; recap of "interpretation, not copies" (version-neutral: the gate, the cast tower, the halved stair, the monastery, Andalusia, the Riaza layout); DATED: the village's hundredth in May 2029 and the Exhibition centenary; before you go (town hall photographs, the glassblower at 81, FIESTA, the Fran Daurel Museum); the arcade (ARQ20: Sangüesa's porticoes; house number not tied to it); out by the Ávila gate.
tracks.listen: Why a village built to be knocked down is still here, the whole visit gathered up, and the way out by the Ávila gate.
